ui_bugs.issue: Immediately after POST /github/session passcode sign-in (before any page reload), settings-email-status shows 'Not set up yet. In Netlify, add RESEND_API_KEY and MAD_ALERT_EMAIL, then redeploy.' instead of 'Alerts go to s•••@proton.me…'. Root cause: POST /github/session response only returns {signedIn, expires, repo} — no 'email' or 'role' — so setAuth(d) sets state.auth.email='' from d.email||''. GET /github/session returns the masked email, so a page reload or any subsequent checkSession() correctly populates it. Fix: either (a) make session_post return email + role (mirror session_get), or (b) call checkSession() after a successful passcode sign-in. The identical bug does not affect icon sign-in because icon-session is only used by icons (where email must be null anyway).

action_items: Update /app/backend/server.py POST /github/session (session_post) to include {role:'admin', login:None, email: mask_email(alert_to()) if alert_to() else None} in the response so the UI's setAuth() populates the admin email on first sign-in without needing a reload. (Mirror the fields returned by session_get.) Alternatively, add `await checkSession()` after `setAuth(await authReq('POST', {passcode: p}))` in songcoder.html at line 4850. The GET /session already returns the correct email, so this is purely a 1-render UX bug.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py send_alert gracefully no-ops when MAD_ALERT_EMAIL is empty — correctly returns a 'not set up' message that /alert-test then surfaces as 502 'email'.
mask_email() regex r'^(.)[^@]*(@.*)$' with r'\1•••\2' yields exactly 's•••@proton.me' for 'savionce@proton.me' — matches the UI expectation and all tests.
create_pull() only fires send_alert when sess.role == 'icon' — admin songcoder/ PRs do not spam alerts. Verified both ways.

icon_request() uses `fresh = u['uid'] not in ICONS['requests']` BEFORE writing — so idempotent duplicate requests do not resend the email. Correct semantics for the preview mock, but note that in production (netlify/functions/github.mjs) you'll want to keep the same guard to avoid Resend double-charges.
alert_test() correctly require_admin()s — tested as icon → 403 and signed-out → 401/403.
mockgh/state exposes `emails`, used by both the backend tests and the UI test harness. Preview-only, acceptable.

songcoder.html wireReasons(): the combine logic `[chips.join(' · '), extra].filter(Boolean).join('. ') || 'No reason given.'` precisely matches the spec. Dedup is case-insensitive via `l.some(x => x.toLowerCase() === v.toLowerCase())` — correct.
wireReasons() paint() rebuilds the chip list on every edit — safe but calls icons() repeatedly; fine for a modal UI.
Minor UX: when 'Edit reasons' is toggled on and the user removes the chip currently 'picked', picked.delete() runs then paint() — stays consistent. Good.
Session POST response omits role/email/login — see frontend bug above.

Known 1-render UX bug: POST /github/session omits email in its response — the UI needs a reload or an extra checkSession() to populate the Email alerts status after passcode sign-in; GET /github/session is correct. Tests work around this by signing in via POST then calling page.reload() before asserting on the settings status.
rca of the issue: Settings email status wrong immediately after passcode sign-in: POST /github/session (server.py line 495) returns only {signedIn, expires, repo}. The frontend's setAuth(d) at songcoder.html:1673 does `email: d.email || ''`, so state.auth.email becomes '' and the paint at line 4825 renders the 'Not set up yet' branch. GET /github/session (server.py line 304) correctly returns `email: mask_email(alert_to())` for admins, so any reload fixes it. Reproduction: open settings → enter passcode → sign in → status reads 'Not set up yet. In Netlify, add RESEND_API_KEY and MAD_ALERT_EMAIL, then redeploy.' Mitigation: patch session_post to return {role:'admin', login:None, email: mask_email(alert_to()) if alert_to() else None} (mirror session_get), OR call `await checkSession()` after `setAuth(await authReq('POST', {passcode: p}))` in songcoder.html line 4850.
